data.name: Maintainer
data.Description: A person who changes the dashboard source or the Python package and runs the build and the checks.

data.name: GitHub workflow runner
data.Description: The hosted runner that executes the Python, web and CodeQL workflows on pull requests, pushes to main and a weekly schedule.

data.name: Dashboard bundle
data.Definition: The built static files of the web dashboard, written into the Python package folder so the installed tool can serve them without Node.js. `web/vite.config.ts:15`

data.name: Dev proxy
data.Definition: The Vite development server setting that forwards requests starting with /api to the Python server on port 8420. `web/vite.config.ts:21`

data.name: API-equivalent cost
data.Definition: What logged usage would have cost at published API list prices, the figure LocalTokenomics reports. `pyproject.toml:4`

data.name: A type error stops the dashboard build
data.Statement: The web build script runs the TypeScript check before Vite, so a type error prevents a bundle from being written.

data.name: A production build replaces the committed bundle
data.Statement: Every production build empties the output folder inside the Python package before writing the new bundle.

data.name: Lint skips build output
data.Statement: ESLint ignores the local dist folder and the bundle inside the Python package.

data.name: Python code must keep a pylint score of 9.0
data.Statement: Both the Python workflow and the pre-commit hook fail when pylint scores below 9.0.

refs.quote: run: uv run --no-sync pylint src tests --fail-under=9.0

data.name: Web dependencies are installed from the lockfile
data.Statement: The web workflow installs with npm ci, which installs exactly what package-lock.json records.

data.name: Python version support
data.Statement: The package supports Python 3.11 or newer and the workflow tests 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 on Ubuntu and Windows.

data.Risk: Mypy is a manual pre-commit stage, so type errors in the Python package are caught only by the workflow or a deliberate local run.
data.Mitigation: The Python workflow runs mypy on src for every pull request.

Rebuild the dashboard bundle
data.Description: A maintainer changes the dashboard source and rebuilds the bundle that the Python package serves.
data.Preconditions: Node.js and npm are installed and dependencies are installed in the web folder.
data.Postconditions: The output folder inside the Python package holds the new bundle.
Main flow: 1. The maintainer runs the build script from the web folder. `web/package.json:8`
2. The TypeScript check runs first and a type error stops the build. `web/package.json:8`
3. Vite writes the bundle into the Python package folder after emptying it. `web/vite.config.ts:16`
data.Alternative flows: 2a. A type error stops the build and no bundle is written. `web/package.json:8`
data.Acceptance criteria: The bundle is written to the folder the package ships. `web/vite.config.ts:15`
data.Special requirements: Asset paths are relative so the bundle loads from whatever URL the server mounts it on. `web/vite.config.ts:7`
rules: A type error stops the dashboard build
A production build replaces the committed bundle

data.name: Develop the dashboard against live data
data.Description: A maintainer runs the dashboard dev server, which forwards API requests to the Python server.
data.Preconditions: The Python server is running on port 8420.
data.Postconditions: The dev server shows the dashboard with live data.
Main flow: 1. The maintainer starts the dev server with the dev script. `web/package.json:7`
2. The dev server listens on port 5173. `web/vite.config.ts:19`
3. Requests starting with /api are forwarded to the Python server. `web/vite.config.ts:22`
data.Alternative flows: 3a. The proxy target is the local server only, so with no Python server running the API requests get no answer. `web/vite.config.ts:22`
data.Acceptance criteria: The dev server answers on its own port and proxies the API path. `web/vite.config.ts:23`

data.name: Check a change before merge
data.Description: A pull request triggers the Python, web and CodeQL workflows, which run the same checks a maintainer runs locally.
data.Preconditions: A pull request is opened or main is pushed.
data.Postconditions: Each workflow reports pass or fail.
Main flow: 1. The workflows start on a pull request or a push to main. `.github/workflows/python.yml:6`
2. The Python workflow runs ruff, pylint, mypy and pytest. `.github/workflows/python.yml:54`
3. The web workflow lints, type checks, tests and builds. `.github/workflows/web.yml:46`
4. CodeQL analyses Python and JavaScript or TypeScript. `.github/workflows/codeql.yml:25`
data.Alternative flows: 2a. A failure in one Python version and operating system pair does not cancel the others. `.github/workflows/python.yml:20`
data.Special requirements: CodeQL also runs weekly on Monday. `.github/workflows/codeql.yml:8`
rules: Python code must keep a pylint score of 9.0
